post_message: In some parts of the world, vaccination can seem like a secondary concern as parents grapple with other tough issues. As one mother told Angu Glory, Cameroon Baptist Convention Health Services (CBCHS) Project District Officer: “There is no need for the vaccine because hunger will kill my child before any vaccine-preventable disease does.”  That comment reflects the harsh reality caregivers in this region face. “Families aren’t rejecting vaccines. They’re frustrated and overwhelmed by the daily struggles to survive,” Glory said.   Recognizing this issue, health workers in the area sought to improve vaccine uptake while helping families meet those additional needs.   The impact was immediate More than 160,000 children were vaccinated, more than 68,000 were screened for malnutrition, over 1,000 received mosquito nets, and more than 13,000 caregivers received practical education on nutrition and vaccines.
